source.verbatim_statement: Let \(S\) be a semialgebraic set in \(\mathbb R^k\), and let \(\theta:\mathbb R^k\to\mathbb R^\ell\) be a semialgebraic map. Then \(\theta(S)\) is semialgebraic in \(\mathbb R^\ell\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Basu and Mishra, Computational and Quantitative Real Algebraic Geometry, Handbook of Discrete and Computational Geometry, 3rd ed. (2017), Theorem 37.2.1, PDF p. 5 / printed p. 974, at the supplied URL. Mathematical glyphs are normalized to LaTeX in this source field.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Suppose \(K=4\), \(m_*\le1/4\), \(0\) and \(1\) are distinct elements of \(\mathcal X\), and \(\rho(0)=1\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), the response-type masses in \(\texttt{def:k4-legal-array}\) are nonnegative, sum to one in each positive-probability covariate cell, satisfy conditional instrument independence, treatment and selected-outcome consistency, global no-defiers, the declared cellwise weak selection monotonicity, fair-instrument overlap, and the aggregate mass floor; hence \(Q_n^{(4)}\in\mathcal M\) and the displayed table is exactly \(p_n^{(4)}\). Its unconditional capacities are \(H_0=(1-r_n)(\ell^0,h^0)\) and \(H_1=r_n(\ell^1,h^1)\). The emerging-cell upper cuts are exactly \((.40,.30,.30,.40)\), so two cuts bind simultaneously; its lower and upper benefit masses are \(0\) and \(.30\), while the main-cell masses are \(0\) and \(.20\). The table contains the selected outcome atom \(p_n^{(4)}(0,0;0,1,0)=\lambda_{\mathrm r}/n\), and \[M(p_n^{(4)})=.25+.25r_n,\qquad \Phi(p_n^{(4)})=\left(0,\frac{.8+.4r_n}{1+r_n}\right).\] For either \(a_n=n^{-1/3}\) or \(a_n=n^{-0.49}\), the specific-array legal envelope has \(c_n\to_P\sqrt{1.28}z_{1-\alpha/2}\), the fallback probability tends to zero, \(P_n\{\Phi(p_n^{(4)})\in C_n\}\to1-\alpha\), and \[\sqrt n\{U(\widehat p_n)-U(p_n^{(4)})\}\Rightarrow N(0,1.28),\] where \(U(\widehat p_n)\) denotes the second coordinate of \(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(\widehat p_n)\). The variance follows from the limiting main-cell ratio: its numerator event has probability \(.10\), its denominator event has probability \(.125\), and \(\{.10(.2)^2+.025(.8)^2\}/.125^2=1.28\); the emerging cell contributes deterministic root-\(n\) drift but only \(o_P(1)\) centered root-\(n\) noise.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: As frozen, the construction is not well typed unless the covariate labels 0 and 1 belong to \(\mathcal X\), and it violates \texttt{ass:cellwise-selection-monotonicity} when \(\rho(0)=-1\) because the main cell has strictly positive selection-gain mass. The proposed statement is a genuine restriction of the same legal model, not a substituted class, and the emerging cell satisfies either sign because its selections are equal.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The derivative-existence proof uses overlap to exclude a single empty instrument arm in a positive covariate cell and the aggregate mass floor for the final quotient; these frozen assumptions must be explicit dependencies.

proposed.statement: The total division operation \(\oslash\) and each coordinate of \(H_x\) are finite semialgebraic functions, while \(F_L\), \(F_U\), and \(m\) are continuous, positively homogeneous, globally Lipschitz, and piecewise linear on a finite polyhedral complex over all of \(\mathbb R^{2K}\). For every \(b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\), \(d_b(g)=\partial_+\bar\Phi(b;g)\) exists and is finite: ordinary quotient rules apply to positive instrument cells, while positive homogeneity together with \(u\oslash0=0\) supplies the ray derivative at empty cells. The map \((b,g)\mapsto d_b(g)\) is jointly semialgebraic and Borel on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\times\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\).
proposed.justification: Finite capacity geometry is the reduction that avoids division by vanishing cell-specific survivor masses.
proposed.gap: Generic directional-delta results do not supply the zero-cell rational limit or the model-specific finite capacity-face decomposition.
proposed.consumer: The legal-face optimizer can enumerate all support and tie configurations needed for reproducible calibration.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The curved-path comparison at an empty cell uses instrument overlap, and its final quotient uses the aggregate mass floor; the proof spine must name both frozen assumptions.

proposed.statement: If \(b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(p:[0,\eta)\to\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is a one-sided differentiable legal path with \(p(0)=b\), then \(\dot p(0+)\in\mathcal D_b\). For every \(g\in\mathcal D_b\) that is generated by such a legal path, \(d_b(g)\) equals the genuine one-sided derivative \(\partial_+\Phi\{p(t)\}|_{t=0}\). Thus values of \(d_b\) outside \(\mathcal D_b\) provide a total calibration convention but no ambient-to-legal realization theorem.
proposed.justification: The domain lemma separates derivatives of legal observed-law paths from algebraic directions introduced solely to make calibration total.
proposed.gap: Generic directional calculus does not identify which zero-cell scores arise from the binary-instrument causal-law image.
proposed.consumer: The legal realization argument can target exactly the admissible tangent scores without claiming an invalid ambient lift.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses the classical Tarski--Seidenberg image theorem, so the cited leaf must be declared in the proof spine.

proposed.statement: The legal observed-law image \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is compact and semialgebraic. For each \(n\), the graph over \(\widehat p\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\) of \(\widehat p\mapsto\{b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}:\|b-\widehat p\|_\infty\le a_n\}\) is compact and semialgebraic; for each fixed \(r>0\), the graph of \(p\mapsto\mathcal B(p,r)\) is compact and semialgebraic. Consequently definable optimization makes \(T_n(g)\) and \(E_{p,r}(g)\) finite Borel value functions of all displayed arguments. With \(G^*=\Sigma(\widehat p_n)^{1/2}W^*\) and the lower-quantile convention, \(c_n\) and the total rectangle \(C_n\) are measurable.
proposed.justification: The confidence procedure requires finite optimizers and a measurable conditional critical value on every empirical law.
proposed.gap: Directional-bootstrap papers typically impose measurability of the derivative process rather than deriving it from this finite legal semialgebraic image.
proposed.consumer: The theorem-level rectangle becomes a genuine statistic suitable for simulation and coverage analysis.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This metadata replacement carries the narrowed witness conditions and declares the newly used covariate-support and selection-direction symbols.

proposed.justification: The proposition is a fully reproducible destructive check in the smallest array containing a rare observed atom, root-\(n\) support emergence, simultaneous cuts, and a degenerate lower endpoint.
proposed.gap: No cited paper verifies common-Gaussian legal-face calibration on a survivor-complier array combining an order-\(n^{-1}\) observed atom, order-\(n^{-1/2}\) support emergence, simultaneous ties, and a degenerate endpoint.
proposed.consumer: A certified legal-face implementation gains an exact atom-level regression test before attempting the full uniform theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the displayed uniform relative comparison between the empirical endpoint error and the conditional quantile of the legal inner-neighborhood envelope when that quantile may converge to zero.
open_obligations.obstruction: The empirical segment from \(p_n\) to \(\widehat p_n\) need not remain in the nonconvex legal observed-law image. The finite capacity-face fundamental-theorem argument therefore supplies ambient or capacity bases, not the legal observed-law bases used by \(E_{p_n,a_n/2}\). Absolute Gaussian coupling error is also insufficient when the envelope quantile vanishes; a relative legal realization bound or a local-flatness certificate is still missing.
open_obligations.attempted: I checked the finite sign/cut decomposition, the exact legal tangent domain, positive-cell quotient bounds, empty-cell homogeneous ray formulas, common-square-root multinomial Gaussian coupling, and the nearby-base padding mechanism on an unseen rare atom. These routes prove fixed-scale regular faces, tight critical values, and the explicit \(K=4\) array, but they do not establish legal capacity-derivative domination uniformly over every irregular array.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Complete the uniform coverage proof by supplying the unresolved legal relative-comparison premise.
open_obligations.obstruction: The theorem's only nonroutine probability bound is exactly \(\texttt{oeq:legal-relative-comparison}\), which remains unproved. Treating that OEQ as established would be circular, and neither endpoint-wise Bonferroni nor an absolute directional delta method controls the stated vanishing-scale arrays.
open_obligations.attempted: I proved the deterministic inner-neighborhood inclusion on the high-probability event \(\|\widehat p_n-p_n\|_\infty\le a_n/2\), the resulting conditional-quantile ordering, and the uniformly negligible fallback probability. This reduces coverage exactly to the unresolved OEQ and no further.
